name: Vertical chin lengthening

card.summary: Genioplasty (or a graft or implant) that makes the chin taller rather than just more forward; documented in the surgical literature, mostly as small case series.
card.aka: Lengthening genioplasty, vertical genioplasty, chin lengthening
card.note: Techniques using grafts carry infection, donor-site and bone-resorption risks described in the literature.

quick.overview:
Vertical chin lengthening is a set of surgical methods that increase the height of the chin, usually by cutting the chin bone and inserting a graft or spacer, or by using an implant. Surgeons describe it for short lower faces, including in East Asian contouring surgery.

The published evidence is largely technique descriptions and case series rather than controlled trials.
quick.mechanism: In an osseous genioplasty the chin segment is cut, moved down, and held in place, with a bone graft or other material filling the gap. Variants combine lengthening with narrowing. Alloplastic implants can also add height.
quick.risks: The literature mentions infection, donor-site problems and resorption of grafted bone as drawbacks of graft-based methods. It is a surgical procedure performed by licensed surgeons.

lead: Vertical chin lengthening is a group of surgical methods that make the chin taller, as distinct from moving it forward. A taller chin lengthens a short lower third of the face, can deepen or soften the relationship between the chin, lower lip and the groove beneath it, and rebalances the profile in people whose chins are short, wide or flat. Methods in the literature include cutting the chin bone and inserting a graft or spacer, redesigning the cut so no graft is needed, and placing an implant [1][2][3][6][19].

Surgeons describe the operation for patients with a vertically short chin (vertical microgenia), the short face syndrome, or a short and wide lower face, with much of the recent literature from East Asia, where it is often combined with narrowing of the chin [1][2][10][12]. A 1987 review discusses lengthening and shortening of the chin by adding or removing bone and states that results improved with miniplate fixation [3].

The published evidence is technique papers and retrospective case series, many with 7 to 38 patients, reporting mostly satisfied patients and few serious complications [6][10][11][12]. No randomized trials of vertical chin lengthening were found [4][5].

chain: Chin bone is cut and lowered, or an implant adds height
Graft, spacer or the repositioned bone fills the gap
Longer chin and lower third of the face, with changed lip-chin balance
angle.text: A surgeon lengthens the chin by repositioning bone with a graft or by adding an implant, which raises the height of the lower face. People who choose it usually have a short or wide chin and want a more proportionate lower third.

paras: In sagittal chin surgery the chin moves forward or back. Vertical surgery changes its height. Vertical deficiency can occur alone or with a receding chin, and the surgical choice depends on the type of deformity and the shape of the labiomental sulcus, the groove between lip and chin [11]. A 2004 review recommended considering vertical lengthening for patients with a vertically short lower face, a deepened labiomental fold, a recessive chin, and a recessive or procumbent lower lip [11].

Other chin procedures covered under the broader heading of genioplasty include sliding genioplasty, which moves a horseshoe-shaped piece of the lower mandible forward or back and fixes it with titanium plates and screws, and implants placed through an incision under the chin or inside the lower lip [19].

A 1987 review of altering the vertical dimension of the chin discusses subtraction and addition of bone, and describes a preferred technique using an interpositional bone graft from the outer table of the calvarium [3]. Earlier reports describe interpositional lengthening for the short face syndrome in 1980 and 1981 [15][5], and a 1988 series of eight patients used a transverse symphyseal osteotomy with hydroxyapatite interposition, with stability at about 11 months [16].

A study of 19 patients who had chin lengthening with allogenic iliac corticocancellous graft during orthognathic surgery reported a mean vertical lengthening of 7 mm (range 4 to 10 mm) with a mean 2 mm horizontal advancement, and no infection, sequestra, fibrous union or reoperation [7].

A 2013 paper describes a pedicled interpositional graft from discarded bone of a narrowing osteotomy for the short, wide lower face, aimed at reducing infection, donor-site problems and loss of height from graft resorption; it reported satisfactory aesthetic results in 32 patients [2]. A 2014 paper from East Asia describes a novel narrowing and lengthening genioplasty intended to avoid the disadvantages of autogenous bone grafts or alloplastic materials [1].

A 2020 paper presents a single-osteotomy technique that requires no interposed bone graft and reports good aesthetic and morphometric outcomes at one year in seven patients [6]. A 2021 paper describes a home plate-shaped sliding osteotomy that can narrow the chin and also lengthen it vertically [17]. A 2023 report of a modified M-shaped genioplasty used narrowing plus vertical elongation in 38 patients [12].

A 2017 report describes advancing and lengthening genioplasty for receding, short chins in 26 patients, planned with CT scans [10]. 'Himi-lengthening' genioplasty is a modified technique used with orthognathic surgery to correct mandibular asymmetry [14], and a 2025 retrospective study compared it with conventional genioplasty [13]. The T-osteotomy, or 'mini V-line', designed by Korean surgeons, removes a trapezoid of bone, reattaches the remaining pieces with titanium plates, and is reported to lengthen the chin by an average of 2 to 3 mm; the mentalis muscle must be carefully reattached [19].

Chin implants of silicone, porous polyethylene (Medpor) or ePTFE can add height as well as projection, and injectable fillers such as hyaluronic acid and calcium hydroxyapatite are used non-surgically for temporary changes [19]. Silicone implants may shift or cause bone resorption beneath them, while porous implants integrate with tissue and are harder to remove [19].

Published studies are technique descriptions and retrospective case series. A review of 262 consecutive osseous genioplasties with bimaxillary surgery reported outcomes and complications of osseous genioplasty in general [4]. In a 2004 retrospective review of 21 patients with vertical microgenia who had lengthening genioplasty with or without grafting, subjective analysis suggested substantial improvement of lower-face aesthetics in all patients and no significant complications [11].

In the 2023 modified M-genioplasty series, vertical lengthening averaged 3.02 mm (range 2 to 5 mm) and narrowing averaged 5.6 mm; chin-satisfaction scores on the FACE-Q rose from 35.34 to 72.95 at three months, with no severe complications over 3 to 24 months [12]. The 2017 series of 26 patients reported that all were satisfied and none had severe complications over at least three months [10].

A 2025 retrospective study of 23 patients compared 13 who had himi-lengthening genioplasty with 10 who had conventional genioplasty for one year, measuring lip and chin sensation, symmetry, segment volume and bone absorption; the himi group had a better mandibular similarity index at one year and segment stability did not differ [13]. No controlled trials of vertical lengthening were identified.

The authors of the pedicled-graft paper list infection, donor-site morbidity and height loss through graft resorption as problems of conventional graft methods [2]. General genioplasty complications include swelling, hematoma and temporary lip numbness; less common ones are infection, implant displacement and nerve damage, and surgeon experience is reported to reduce risk [19]. In the 2025 comparison, two-point discrimination on the lip and chin changed on days 1 and 4 after surgery but not significantly at 1 and 3 months [13]. Donor bone from the rib or ilium appears linked to higher infection rates [19][9].
A 2026 retrospective cohort examined the effect of aesthetic osseous genioplasty on upper airway volumes [8].

Vertical lengthening appears in looksmaxxing discussion under the 'hardmaxxing' heading for surgical changes to bone. A looksmax.org thread asks whether to choose a vertical lengthening chin implant or a vertical lengthening genioplasty for a taller chin, and also asks how much PSL (a facial-rating scale used on the forum) it would add; a reply shows a Facetune morph of a chin made taller only [18].

timeline.event: Interpositional lengthening genioplasty for the short face syndrome is reported [15].
A review of shortening and lengthening the chin reports improved results with miniplate fixation and calvarial grafts [3].
A series of eight patients with vertically deficient chins is treated with symphyseal osteotomy and hydroxyapatite interposition [16].
A review of 21 patients with vertical microgenia reports improved lower-face aesthetics [11].
Pedicled interpositional graft for narrowing and lengthening genioplasty is described [2].
A novel narrowing and lengthening genioplasty is published [1].
A retrospective review examines chin lengthening with allogenic iliac graft [7].
Advancing and lengthening genioplasty is reported in 26 patients with receding, short chins [10].
A single-osteotomy technique for vertical lengthening genioplasty is described [6].
A modified M-genioplasty series reports narrowing plus vertical lengthening in 38 patients [12].
A long-term retrospective study of himi-lengthening genioplasty is published [13].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org the topic appears mainly as a choice between a vertical implant and a bone-cutting genioplasty for a taller chin, often with questions about how much it would improve a rating [18].

claims.claim: A taller chin noticeably improves facial harmony.
claims.believers: A forum poster asks how much PSL a vertical lengthening would bring, and another uses a Facetune morph of a chin made taller only to illustrate the change [18].
claims.experts: A 2004 review of 21 patients reported subjective improvement of lower-face aesthetics in all, and a 2023 series reported higher FACE-Q chin satisfaction at three months; no controlled trials exist [11][12].

claims.claim: Implant or genioplasty can both deliver vertical height.
claims.believers: The thread frames the two operations as alternatives for a taller chin [18].
claims.experts: Surgical sources describe both implants and bone-cutting methods for chin height, with implants carrying displacement and resorption risks and graft methods carrying infection and resorption risks [19][2].
